questions.question: An engineer deposits \( \$4,000 \) into an account earning an effective annual interest rate of \( 6\% \). Approximately how many years will it take for the account balance to reach \( \$8,000 \)?

A service vehicle is purchased for \( \$30,000 \). It is expected to be kept for \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \), after which it will have a salvage value of \( \$5,000 \). If the interest rate is \( 8\% \), what is the equivalent uniform annual cost of owning the vehicle?

A new manufacturing process will save a company \( \$20,000 \) per year for \( 8 \, \mathrm{years} \). Additionally, at the end of year 8, the equipment can be sold for a salvage value of \( \$15,000 \). If the interest rate is \( 10\% \), what is the total present worth of these benefits?

A bridge will require a major refurbishment costing \( \$50,000 \) per year for 4 consecutive years, with the first payment occurring at the end of year 6 (i.e., payments at the end of years 6, 7, 8, and 9). If the interest rate is \( 4\% \), what is the present worth of these costs at year 0?

A gradient series has a base amount of \( \$0 \) in year 1 and increases by \( \$1,000 \) each year through year 6. If the interest rate is \( 6\% \), what is the future worth of this gradient series at the end of year 6?

An operating expense is expected to be \( \$5,000 \) in year 1, and will increase by \( \$500 \) each subsequent year through year 8. If the interest rate is \( 8\% \), what is the equivalent uniform annual expense over the \( 8 \)-year period?

The maintenance cost for a machine is \( \$1,000 \) at the end of the first year, and increases by \( \$200 \) each year thereafter for a total of \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). If the interest rate is \( 10\% \), what is the present worth of these maintenance costs?

A firm needs to accumulate \( \$150,000 \) in \( 8 \, \mathrm{years} \) to replace manufacturing equipment. If the account earns an annual interest rate of \( 5.5\% \), what uniform annual deposit is required at the end of each year?
An engineer invests \( \$5,000 \) in an index fund that is expected to return exactly \( 7.5\% \) per year. What is the expected future worth of this investment after \( 12 \, \mathrm{years} \)?

A city plans to upgrade its water treatment plant in \( 15 \, \mathrm{years} \) at an estimated cost of \( \$2,000,000 \). If the city can earn \( 4\% \) annually on its investments, how much must be deposited today to exactly fund this future upgrade?
A construction company purchases a new tractor for \( \$45,000 \). If the annual interest rate is \( 8\% \), what is the equivalent uniform annual cost of this investment over a \( 10 \)-year period?

A civil engineer deposits \( \$10,000 \) into a savings account that pays an effective annual interest rate of \( 6\% \). What is the approximate future worth of the account after \( 8 \, \mathrm{years} \)?

A company bought a vehicle for $50,000. The expected life span is 10 years, the expected salvage value is $10,000, and the annual maintenance expenditure is $1,500. If the interest rate is 6% per year, find the present worth of the total cost.
Initial cost: \(P_0=\$50{,}000\)

Annual maintenance: \(A=\$1{,}500/\text{yr}\) for \(n=10\) years

Salvage value at year 10: \(F_S=\$10{,}000\)

Interest rate: \(i=6\% \)

A project will require $100,000 to be paid 5 years from now. If the annual interest rate i is 6%,

how much money should be deposited each year (end of year) so the fund reaches $100,000 at year 5?
Future requirement: \(F=\$100{,}000\) at \(n=5\)

Interest rate: \(i=6\%=0.06\)

Unknown: equal annual deposit \(A\) (sinking fund)

Using the data below, determine the account balance (future value) after 6 years.
Initial deposit (present value): \(P = \$1{,}200\)

Annual interest rate: \(i = 6\%\) (compounded annually)

Time: \(n = 6\) years

With an annual interest rate of \( 10\% \) compounded annually, determine the project’s equivalent annual worth. The equivalent annual worth is most nearly:
An investment account offers a nominal annual interest rate of \( 6\% \), compounded daily. Assuming \( 365 \) days in a year, what is the annual effective interest rate?
A credit card charges a nominal annual interest rate of \( 18\% \), compounded monthly. What is the annual effective interest rate?

An initial investment of \( \$60,000 \) is expected to produce the following uneven net cash flows: Year 1: \( \$10,000 \); Year 2: \( \$15,000 \); Year 3: \( \$20,000 \); Year 4: \( \$25,000 \). What is the approximate payback period for this investment?

A company invests \( \$120,000 \) in new automated packaging equipment. The equipment is expected to generate a constant net annual savings of \( \$24,000 \). Ignoring the time value of money, what is the simple payback period for this investment?

A manufacturing plant has a maximum production capacity of \( 50,000 \) units per year. The fixed annual expenses for the plant are \( \$300,000 \). The variable expense to produce each unit is \( \$12 \), and each unit is sold for \( \$20 \). What is the breakeven percentage of capacity of operation?

Two machines are being considered for a manufacturing process. Machine A has an initial cost of \( \$5,000 \) and provides annual savings of \( \$1,400 \) for \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). Machine B has an initial cost of \( \$7,000 \) and provides annual savings of \( \$1,900 \) for \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). At approximately what interest rate would the two machines be equally economical?

A company manufactures widgets. The fixed costs for the manufacturing plant are \( \$20,000 \) per month. The variable cost to produce each widget is \( \$15 \), and each widget is sold for \( \$25 \). What is the breakeven volume of widgets that must be produced and sold per month to exactly cover total expenses?

A firm is considering adopting an alternative method to replace its current method for producing a specific part. Ignoring the time value of money, estimate the payback time (years) for adopting the proposed method.
Current method unit cost: $1.80 per unit

Proposed method unit cost: $0.70 per unit

One-time implementation cost (proposed): $32,500

Expected annual production volume: 8,000 units
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5 P230:

Engineering Economics – Breakeven Analysis

questions.question: An engineer is evaluating an investment of \( \$10,000 \) today. The project is expected to last \( 4 \, \mathrm{years} \). If the interest rate is \( 6\% \) per year and the general inflation rate is \( 2\% \) per year, what is the approximate future worth of this investment?

A company anticipates a future expense of \( \$25,000 \) in exactly \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). If the standard interest rate is \( 5\% \) per year and the general inflation rate is \( 3\% \) per year, what is the approximate present worth of this future expense?

A project has an expected standard interest rate of \( 7\% \) per year. If the general inflation rate is estimated to be \( 4\% \) per year, what is the inflation-adjusted interest rate per interest period?

A piece of equipment currently valued at \( \$6,500 \) was purchased \( 4 \, \mathrm{years} \) ago. It incurs an annual maintenance cost of \( \$320 \). Over those \( 4 \, \mathrm{years} \), the average inflation rate was \( 4.5\% \), and the effective annual interest rate was \( 5.5\% \). What was the approximate uninflated (real) worth of the equipment when it was purchased?

A manufacturing facility purchases automated assembly equipment with an initial cost of \( \$100,000 \). The equipment qualifies for a \( 7 \)-year MACRS recovery period. What is the expected depreciation amount for this equipment in year \( 6 \)?
A civil engineering firm purchases surveying equipment for \( \$80,000 \). The equipment falls under the \( 5 \)-year MACRS recovery period. What is the expected depreciation amount in year \( 3 \)?

A piece of construction equipment has an initial cost of \( \$50,000 \). It has an expected useful life of \( 8 \, \mathrm{years} \) and an expected salvage value of \( \$10,000 \). Using the straight-line method, what is the depreciation amount for the third year?

A company bought a vehicle for \( $50{,}000 \). The expected life span is 10 years, and the expected salvage value is \( $10{,}000 \).

What is the total depreciation in the first 3 years using the straight-line method?
Initial cost: \(C=\$50{,}000\)

Salvage value: \(S_n=\$10{,}000\)

Service life: \(n=10\ \text{years}\)

Years considered: \(j=3\)

A company purchases a equipment with the cost of \($12{,}500\) .

Using the Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System (MACRS) with a 10-year recovery period, determine the total depreciation during the first 3 years of operation. (Interest and maintenance do not affect MACRS depreciation,

but are provided for context.)
Initial cost: \(P=\$12{,}500\)

Annual interest rate: \(3\%\)

Annual maintenance (paid at year end): \(\$420\)

Engineering Economics – Depreciation – MACRS

questions.question:
A company purchased a equipment with the cost of \($12{,}500\) .

Using the Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System (MACRS) with a 10-year recovery period, determine the book value after the first 3 years of operation. (Interest and maintenance do not affect MACRS depreciation,

but are provided for context.)
Initial cost: \(P=\$12{,}500\)

Annual interest rate: \(3\%\)

Annual maintenance (paid at year end): \(\$420\)

An equipment has a useful life of \( 10 \, \mathrm{years} \), an initial cost of \( \$4,000 \), and a salvage value of \( \$1,200 \). The interest rate is \( 3\% \). Using the straight-line method, determine the total depreciation of the equipment for the first \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). The total depreciation is most nearly:

A company purchased a piece of heavy equipment with an initial cost of \( \$10,000 \). The annual interest rate is \( 2.5\% \). The equipment requires annual maintenance costing \( \$400 \), which is paid at the end of each year. Using the Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System (MACRS), determine the total depreciation for the equipment during the first \( 3 \, \mathrm{years} \) of operation, assuming a \( 10 \)-year recovery period. The total depreciation is most nearly:

An agricultural business purchases a new tractor for \( \$50,000 \). The tractor qualifies for a \( 10 \)-year MACRS recovery period. What is the approximate book value of the tractor at the exact end of the \( 10 \)-year recovery period (end of year \( 10 \))?

A company buys computer software with an initial cost of \( \$60,000 \). It qualifies for a \( 3 \)-year MACRS recovery period. What is the approximate book value of the software at the end of year \( 2 \)?

A manufacturing plant purchases a new machine for \( \$120,000 \). The machine has an estimated salvage value of \( \$20,000 \) after its \( 10 \)-year useful life. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the book value of the machine at the end of year \( 4 \)?

A corporation has a gross income of \( \$300,000 \) and ordinary operating expenses of \( \$100,000 \) for the current year. During this same year, the corporation purchased new manufacturing equipment for \( \$80,000 \). The equipment qualifies for a \( 5 \)-year MACRS recovery period. If the corporate income tax rate is \( 21\% \), what is the total income tax paid for this first year?

For a given tax year, a business has a total gross income of \( \$200,000 \). The business incurred \( \$60,000 \) in ordinary expenses. Earlier in the year, they purchased a piece of capital equipment for \( \$150,000 \), which has a \( 6 \)-year useful life and a \( \$30,000 \) salvage value. Using the straight-line method for depreciation, what is the taxable income for this first year?

A company bought an equipment for $5,000. The annual maintenance fee is $500 and continues indefinitely. If the interest rate is 5% per year, determine the present worth of all expenditures.
Initial cost: \(P_0=\$5{,}000\)

Annual maintenance: \(A=\$500/\text{yr}\) (perpetuity)

Interest rate: \(i=5\%=0.05\)

A bike was purchased with an initial cost of \( \$1,300 \) and an annual maintenance cost of \( \$250 \), which continues indefinitely. The interest rate is \( 6\% \). Determine the present worth of all expenditures.

A bond has a face value of \( \$5,000 \) and pays a nominal annual coupon rate of \( 6\% \), with payments made semi-annually. The bond matures in \( 10 \, \mathrm{years} \). If the required nominal interest rate is \( 8\% \) per year, what is the approximate value of the bond?

An investor purchases a bond for \( \$8,403 \). The bond has a face value of \( \$10,000 \), pays an annual coupon of \( \$400 \), and matures in \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). What is the approximate computed bond yield (interest rate)?

A bond has a face value of \( \$10,000 \), pays a uniform annual interest coupon of \( 5\% \), and matures in \( 10 \, \mathrm{years} \). If an investor’s required interest rate (yield) is \( 8\% \), what is the approximate value (present worth) of the bond?

An engineer invests \( \$20,000 \) in a long-term savings investment that guarantees a payout of exactly \( \$31,876 \) at the end of \( 8 \, \mathrm{years} \). What is the exact annual rate of return on this investment?

A company is considering a project that requires an initial investment of \( \$50,000 \) and provides uniform annual benefits of \( \$13,000 \) for \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). The company’s Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR) is \( 12\% \). What is the approximate rate of return, and should the project be accepted?

A proposed public park has an initial construction cost of \( \$50,000 \). The present worth of the expected annual public benefits is \( \$80,000 \), and the present worth of the annual maintenance costs is \( \$10,000 \). What is the benefit-cost ratio \( B/C \) for this project?

A construction project has potential weather delay costs with the following probability distribution: a \( 50\% \) chance of \( 0 \) days delay (\( \$0 \) cost), a \( 30\% \) chance of a \( 10 \)-day delay (\( \$10,000 \) cost), a \( 15\% \) chance of a \( 20 \)-day delay (\( \$25,000 \) cost), and a \( 5\% \) chance of a \( 30 \)-day delay (\( \$50,000 \) cost). What is the expected value of the delay cost?

An engineer is evaluating a decision tree with two paths. Path A requires an initial investment of \( \$20,000 \). It leads to a chance node with a \( 60\% \) probability of generating \( \$50,000 \) in revenue and a \( 40\% \) probability of generating \( \$10,000 \) in revenue. Path B requires an initial investment of \( \$10,000 \). It leads to a chance node with a \( 70\% \) probability of generating \( \$30,000 \) in revenue and a \( 30\% \) probability of generating \( \$5,000 \) in revenue. Which decision path should be chosen to maximize expected profit, and what is its expected value?

A business venture has a single chance node with three possible outcomes: a \( 40\% \) probability of a \( \$10,000 \) profit, a \( 35\% \) probability of a \( \$5,000 \) profit, and a \( 25\% \) probability of a \( \$2,000 \) loss. What is the expected value of this venture?
